newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turks seek new petrochemicals investment - official.
newsitem.headline: Turks seek new petrochemicals investment - official.

text.p: Turkey's petrochemicals industry, which grew by 14 percent last year, is in need of new investment to meet growing demand, a senior official said.

"The market grew by 14 percent last year, one of the fastest growths in the world, and consumption rose to 17.5 kilograms per capita," Mehmet Yilmaz, general manager of Petkim Petrokimya Holding A.S., told a news conference.
"But from time to time we cannot meet the demand," he added.
Yilmaz said the market was expected to grow further.
"Continous growth and its geographical location which is very close to the raw material sources make Turkey an attractive base to invest in its petrochemical products industry," Yilmaz said.
He said Turkey needs the establishment of four or five new plants to meet demand at home and in neighbouring countries.

Petkim officials and shareholders complain that the company's new capacity expansion investments are restricted by the privatisation agency OIB, the main shareholder of the company which has been put on the government's sell-off list.
The company has spent 146 billion lira so far in 1997 on modernisation and plans to increase it to 2.76 trillion lira by the end of this year.
Petkim currently meets only about 50 percent of domestic demand.
The company aims to increase turnover to 127 trillion lira in 1997 from 72 trillion lira last year, Yilmaz said.

He expects 23.6 trillion lira of net profit, slightly less than 24.4 trillion lira in 1996 based on assumptions that 1997 inflation will stand at 83 percent and the average dollar rate will be 147,265 lira.
Yilmaz said total sales in foreign currency would be $864.7 million in 1997, including $762.1 million of domestic sales and $102.6 million of exports.
Petkim reported 23.966 trillion lira total sales in the first quarter, against 14.741 trillion lira in the same period of 1996. Net profits dropped to 5.798 trillion from 7.283 trillion.
